page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is an entry-tier virtual cloud instance within the Cloud Compute family. It features 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration relies on an x86_64 architecture with 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance primarily in the lower quartiles of compute and memory throughput. CPU performance registered 1304.17 in stress-ng single-core and 5030.23 in multi-core metrics, both falling into the bottom 25% bracket. Similarly, Geekbench scores reached 1013.0 single-core and 3188.0 multi-core, while PassMark delivered a CPU score of 4794.79. Memory bandwidth tests indicated 367.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 24.41 GB/sec read and 19.55 GB/sec write on uncached large blocks. Workload tests recorded 2.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.09 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The shared CPU provisioning and lower clock frequency present distinct performance constraints under prolonged multi-threaded or compute-heavy loads, where resource contention may arise. However, the bundling of 160 GB NVMe storage provides high local storage density relative to its resource profile. The configuration suits cost-conscious deployments such as light staging environments, background task workers, low-traffic web applications, microservices, and secondary integration testing nodes.
description: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a Cloud Compute virtual instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a single public IPv4 address. Benchmarking reflects entry-tier performance, with single-core and multi-core evaluations consistently placing in the lower percentiles across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. Uncached memory write speeds settle at 19.55 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 3.09 GB/sec. Given its shared CPU allocation and modest clock speeds, sustained intensive computing presents clear bottlenecks. The instance is suitable for budget-conscious general utilities, lightweight web serving, staging servers, and asynchronous background worker tasks.
